en: Okay, thank you!
Thank you! You're a lifesaver.
Yes! I win! Lunch is on you, Ta-chan. Could you get me a Bento Lunch set?
Oh, man... But all right. A promise is a promise.
I'm seriously famished. Run over there if you can, before I starve to death!
All right, I'll scoot off to the convenience store. One Bento Lunch Set's good enough for you?
Of course. One is plenty. Thanks, Ta-chan.
Uh-oh, I lost. Okay, I keep my promises. I'll treat you to some convenience store takeout.
Hahaha, it's not very gallant of me, but it was a fair wager. I'll happily accept that treat.
What should I go buy?
Oden Soup? Okay. I'll be back in a few minutes.
Here you go, Ta-chan.
You got some <Color:8>Oden Soup<Color:Default>.
Bento Lunch Set? Okay. I'll be back in a few minutes.
You got <Color:8>Bento Lunch Set<Color:Default>.
Special Yakisoba? Okay. I'll be back in a few minutes.
Here you go, Ta-chan!
You got some <Color:8>Special Yakisoba<Color:Default>.
Wow, thanks, Mi-chan. You're an angel.
I didn't expect you to be able to hit like that. Pretty impressive, to be honest. But I guess I shouldn't have doubted you!
I'm gonna have to make it harder on you next time!
Oh, boy, don't make it too hard.
Oh, hi, Ta-chan. How are you?
Alright. You don't look so good, though. You doing okay?
Really? I mean, I haven't eaten anything today. I should nip out and get some takeout.
What, and leave the place unattended?
It'll be only a few minutes. I'm just stepping out to grab something quick!
I guess that's true.
Oh, Ta-chan, are you hungry, too?
Huh? What, you gonna treat me to something?
Well... How about maybe?
Want to make a bet of it? We'll see if you can hit a home run off a pitching machine or not.
Hmm... Yeah, I could go for that. Sounds fun.
Okay, how about we base it off three pitches? If you can hit a home run, it'll be my treat.
So naturally, that means that you have to treat me to lunch if you can't do it.
Fine. You know, Mi-chan, I'm pretty good at this batting stuff. You might end up regretting this little bet of yours.
Three pitches is more than plenty for smacking out a homer.
Well, let's see if you have to eat those words... and my lunch bill! Hah!
What would you like to do?
Huh? Who are you?
I just started today. The lady who used to work here suddenly quit, and they had an ad out saying they were hiring, so here I am!
Oh, so the old lady's gone...
(I mean, she did try to kill me...)
Um, are you a regular here?
Huh? Uh, yeah, you might say that.
Oh, then let me introduce myself! I'm Miki Murai. Please feel free to call me Mi-chan.
Okay, Mi-chan. It's nice to see this place get someone so pretty to work the counter. It'll bring some much-needed shine to the establishment.
Haha, thanks!
I'm Tatsuo Shinada. You can call me Ta-chan.
Okay, Ta-chan. Huh? Wait, your face... There's...
What's wrong with my face?
Oh, no, I just think I recognize you from somewhere.
Huh? Really?
Oh! That's it! I think I've seen you in town with someone. Ta-chan, do you maybe know Takasugi-san?
Takasugi-san? As in the money lender? That Takasugi-san?
Yes! That's him.
Mi-chan, why do you know Takasugi-san?
Well, it's, um... Because I borrowed money from him.
Oh, that's what it is. You owe him money, too.
Huh? Come to think of it, I think I heard your name somewhere, too.
What was it now? Was that you on the phone with Takasugi-san?
(Oh, right, Takasugi had her working at a bathhouse to repay her loan. She was crying because her jaw hurt...)
Oh, so that's who you are. You're that Mi-chan!
Oh! Did you hear about me from Takasugi-san, then?
Uh, just a little. Like, you're, uh, working another job? It must be pretty tough for you.
Well, I gotta. If I don't pay back this loan quick, the interest's just gonna keep piling up.
That's so true. We both have to dig down and work.
Ooh, ouch. My jaw hurts.
Are you okay? Don't work yourself too hard.
Yeah, it's nothing...
(Her jaw aches? From working at some sleazy bathhouse, the poor girl. She looks so innocent, too. Some world we live in.)
Okay, Ta-chan. Enjoy your visit. If you need anything, I'm right here.
Oh, hello. Our batting center's machines are pretty tough. If you're just a beginner, you might want to think about heading back out through that door.
So, uh, were you able to check out the snow statue locations?
Oh, geez... I'm sorry, but could I ask you to please hurry? We really need the info right away!
I'd go, but I have to stay in this spot, so please tell me when you figure out where they all are. Thank you!
Are you sure you remember it all correctly?
Yeah. I can tell ya where the snow statues are.
Fantastic! Let's get right to it, while your memory's fresh.
So, looking at the site from here, there's a giant slide. Facing the slide from the front, what's to your right?
Facing the slide, to the right, was a bear.
Okay, the bear. Next one...
Facing the slide, to the right, was a snowman.
A snowman? Somebody entered that?
Saw it with my own eyes.
Uh, right, of course. Sorry, I didn't mean to imply I doubted you. Anyway...
Facing the slide, to the right, was some girl with a wand? Not sure what she's s'posed to be.
Oh, yes, yes, that's right! I remember now. That's the magic girl statue.
Okay, the next one I need to know about...
Which snow statue is right in the middle?
Some seals were smack dab in the middle.
Oh, right, there were seals! This is very helpful.
There was a snow crystal right smack dab in the middle.
A snow crystal? Was there, really? Don't remember that one.
Yeah. No mistake.
I see. A snow crystal right in the middle, huh?
There was a slide right smack dab in the middle.
Hm? No, that can't be right. The slide is one of the giant dioramas flanking the site.
Oh... I guess it was.
Hmm... Maybe you should go check the statues again?
Across from the slide, there's another diorama, a massive one if I recall. What did it feature?
That'd be a treasure ship.
A treasure ship...? My memory must be slipping. I don't remember a treasure ship at all.
That'd be a whale.
Oh yeah. I completely forgot about the whale. Even though it's so big!
That'd be a dragon.
Huh? That's not right. The dragon was a smaller statue. I'm sure.
There's only one statue left to confirm. What was the small one next to the penguin?
A fox.
Ahhh, that's where the fox is. Okay! I know the locations of all the statues now.
I dunno who she is, but it's a girl with her hair in two really long pigtails.
Ah, that would be Hatsune Miku. Of course someone sculpted her; she's such a popular character. Well, you did it! Now I know where all the statues are.
I think it was a dragon.
Oh, that's where the dragon is. Okay! Now I know where all the statues are!
Well, thank you very much! You can't imagine what a big help that was.
Oy! You there!
Yes?
I got the site layout with all the statue locations. It's all on this note, so go have the site map printed, okay?
I'll place an order with the printers now.
Thank you again! We couldn't have done it without you. Please accept this as a souvenir of the event.
You got a <Color:8>Mystery Stone<Color:Default>.
Thanks. And hey, good luck. Lookin' forward to yer snow festival.
Huh? Hold on a second, one of these locations isn't right!
I was on-site earlier, helping with setup. So I remember where at least some of the statues are...
I see. I guess the gentleman here gave me wrong info about one of the statues... which means I can't really trust any other information he brought me...
I'm sorry. I shouldn't have given you this task.
I hope you don't expect a reward. I mean, I know you put in some effort and all, but...
No, forget it. Guess I got a bit confused, there.
No, no, it's my fault...
Should I go take a look at them?
No. I don't feel comfortable delegating anymore. If you want a job done right, you have to do it yourself.
Good luck gettin' it done. Lookin' forward to the snow festival.
Yes, I think we'll really need it now, after this fiasco.
(...Right.)
Why can't people ever do things right?
Oh! Um, I'm the snow festival operations manager. My staff pulled a bonehead move that might ruin everything.
I just learned that no one ordered site maps for the visitors.
If we don't order them right now, the printers won't have enough time, but... Aargh! Darn it!
What's keepin' ya? Order it now.
I'd love to, but my memory is foggy when it comes to which snow statues are at which locations.
And I can't leave my post to go check, and my staff is too busy doing a million other things.
I get it. You're undermanned.
Exactly! You understand. Hey, wait a minute... Maybe you have some spare time?
I hate to impose, but... would you be willing to check the snow statue locations?
I can't pay you, but I could give you a festival souvenir for your efforts. It shouldn't take long, and it would be a huge help.
Don't know. That's askin' a lot.
Oh, please! We're desperate.
So, ya want me to see what statues are on the site and where, right?
Yes! I'll be right here when you come back. I have to be, after all!

Oh, hello. Are you interested in taking Sotenbori Announcer
School's free introductory class? If you have the time,
please give it a try.
Oh, hello. Are you interested in broadcasting, communications, or becoming an announcer? Our school will give you specialized training.

We're the Sotenbori Announcer School, and right now we're
offering a free introductory class!
A free class?

That's right. More than ninety percent of the students
who've graduated from our program have landed broadcasting
or other voice-related jobs.

We've put together a rich curriculum which trains the
broadcasting student in enunciation, intonation, diction,
and proper language usage.
Are you interested in becoming an announcer?
Me? Not really, no...

Our course is perfect for anyone who wants to work in a
voice-related field⑬voice actors, TV talent, narrators,
presenters, etc.
Oh, I see.

(Hmm. A lot of those skills sound like they might be really
helpful in my line of work.)

Would you at least like to try our introductory class? It's
completely free. You can even take it right now, if you have
time.
All right. I'll give it a try.
Wonderful! In that case, come right this way, please.
No, that's all right.

I see. What a shame. Well, if you ever change your mind, you
can come back and see me anytime.
Oh, this gyoza smells so good... Huh? What are you staring at? I'm eating here.

Oh, hello, Sawamura-san. Have you changed your mind? Would
you like to take part in SBR99?

All right. Thank you very much for asking me. I think I'll
give it a try!

Wonderful! I'm very glad to hear it. Your agency is Dyna
Chair, isn't that right? I'll contact them myself to make
the proper arrangements.

Now, if you'll come right this way, I'll show you to the
event hall.
I appreciate the offer, but I'm afraid I'll have to say no.

Ah, that's too bad. But I guess I did ask you out of the
blue. If you ever change your mind, please don't hesitate
to come see me.

Hm? What's up? You up for another dance battle? I can do
that, but it'll cost ya another 1,000 if ya lose.
Sure, you're on.
Good answer! Here we go!

You know, I'd love to, but I'm a little short on funds right
now.

Worried about losin' before ya begin, eh? C'mon, where's
your spine? That said, yes, bring money.
No, I'll pass for now.
Hmph. Well, that's probably for the best.

I'm in shock... My goodness gracious me, ya got some smooth
moves for a man your age.
Maybe, but you're really one to talk.

Tell me, though⑬you're not actually a dancer, are you? The
way you move leads me to believe you're an amateur through
and through.

Oh, is it that obvious? Guess there's no fooling a prima
ballerina. It's like you say, I'm no dancer.

Well, it's truly astonishing, a man with no formal training
dancin' so well.

The way you use your feet, especially. I know pros that
can't even do the things ya do.
...Heh, all right, sonny. You win this one.

I've been dancin' for over half a century. And if an amateur
dances that well against me, I can't, in good conscience,
give myself the win.

That's why this round's yours, sonny. Here, take your 1,000
yen.

Heheh, watchin' you dance was almost like seein' my late
husband dance again. Ya made me remember the old coot.
Heh. That's quite an honor.

Of course, the old coot was a little better lookin' than
you. No offense. See ya!
